rationale: A same-commit envelope cannot declare the tree OID of the commit that contains it (the envelope blob is an input of that tree; writing the envelope changes the tree). v3.2 splits the result into TWO commits per leaf: R (implementation result, parent = C) and E (envelope container, parent = R). The envelope lives ONLY in E, declares OIDs of C and R, and never its own identity. The remote leaf branch points to E; the external binding is recorded by the controller AFTER push in a separate receipt.

ft-<n>.evidence: controller clean-checkout rerun on exact R

required_fields.build_provenance: path to leaf provenance receipt (must match build-provenance-policy-v3.2.json)

validation_rules: envelope ABSENT from R; envelope PRESENT in E
diff C..R limited to implementation/provenance owned paths
diff R..E exactly the single frozen envelope path
remote branch SHA == E after push (recorded externally by the controller; never inside the envelope)
no field may contain the E commit OID, the E tree OID, the envelope blob OID, the envelope SHA-256, or the resolved remote branch SHA

forbidden_self_binding.note: These values are recorded externally by the controller AFTER push, in the external branch-binding receipt.

naming_rule: Git object IDs use the *_commit_oid / *_tree_oid / git_object_format naming; the term 'SHA-256' is NOT used for Git object IDs. Ordinary file hashes keep the suffix '_sha256'.
artifacts_rules: artifacts may contain hashes of files present in R
artifacts may NOT contain the envelope itself
artifacts may NOT contain files added only in E
artifacts may NOT contain the container commit/tree OID
